title: Arise, My Gracious God
description: Arise, My Gracious God in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 17, part 1, headed “Portion of saints and sinners; or, Hope and despair in death”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-rise, my gra-cious God, And make the wi-cked flee; They are but thy cha-stis-ing rod To drive thy saints to thee.

lines: They are but thy chastising rod
To drive thy saints to thee.
Here in this life his pleasure lies,
And boast of all his store:
My soul can wish no more.
Drest in the likeness of thy Son,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
